prose.favour: The case in its favour rests mostly on the recent price trend: the share price is 8.9% higher than a year ago. Also in its favour: over the past year the share did 10.7 percentage points better than the Nifty 50; the share price is close to its 52-week high; and profit covers interest costs 5.4 times over. Other areas on this side: the balance sheet, growth.
prose.against: The case against rests mostly on cash flow and the balance sheet: free cash flow for the last financial year was negative: the business spent more than it generated. Also against it: return on capital employed is only 7.2%, a weak return on the money in the business; the 3-year maximum drawdown was -59.3%, a deep fall; and one-year volatility is 45.4%, high. Other areas on this side: price behaviour, risk, the quality of the business.
prose.weighing: Weighing them: 6 points in favour and 8 against give more points against. The pool score is 34 of 100. The side that carries most weight is cash flow and the balance sheet. That gives an educational rating of Underweight with high confidence. This is a rule-based reading of the evidence above, not a prediction.
